editorial:
Decorated veteran Will Sharp needs money fast for his wife's medical bills, so he turns to his adoptive brother Danny, a smooth-talking criminal. Danny pulls him into a massive Los Angeles bank heist worth $32 million, and everything goes wrong when a cop gets shot. The brothers hijack an ambulance with a wounded officer and a tough paramedic, turning a simple escape into a wild chase across the city. The movie feels loud, tense, and nonstop, with Michael Bay style action and a surprising amount of heart between two brothers who love and frustrate each other.

Jake Gyllenhaal is electric as Danny, while Yahya Abdul-Mateen II gives Will real emotional weight. The action is huge, the camera never stops moving, and the pacing rarely lets you breathe. Some scenes are too long and the dialogue can be silly, but the energy keeps you watching. If you want a smart crime drama, this is not it. If you want a big, messy, exciting ride, it delivers.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, Will and Danny are trapped after a huge chase and shootout. Danny tries to escape by helicopter but is shot and falls to his death. Will survives, saves the wounded cop and paramedic, and is arrested. The movie ends with Will in prison, but his wife gets the medical help she needs, and the paramedic visits him, showing he did the right thing in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves loud, fast action movies and big chase scenes.
